questions.explanationHtml:
Choice B is correct. To find \(35\%\) of 80, convert the percent to a decimal: \(35\% = 0.35\). Then multiply: \(0.35 \times 80 = 28\).

Choice A is incorrect and may result from using \(30\%\) instead of \(35\%\). Choice C is incorrect and may result from using \(37.5\%\) or a miscalculation. Choice D is incorrect and may result from using \(40\%\).

questions.questionHtml: The price of a book increased from $25 to $30. What is the percent increase?
questions.explanationHtml:
Choice C is correct. Percent increase \(= \frac{\text{new - original}}{\text{original}} \times 100\% = \frac{30 - 25}{25} = \frac{5}{25} = 0.20 = 20\%\).

Choice A is incorrect and may result from simply subtracting the two prices without dividing. Choice B is incorrect and may result from dividing by the new price instead of the original. Choice D is incorrect and may result from miscalculating \(5 / 20\).

questions.questionHtml: A shirt originally priced at $40 is on sale for $32. What is the percent decrease?
questions.explanationHtml:
Choice B is correct. Percent decrease \(= \frac{\text{original - new}}{\text{original}} \times 100\% = \frac{40 - 32}{40} = \frac{8}{40} = 0.20 = 20\%\).

Choice A is incorrect and may result from simply finding the dollar decrease without dividing. Choice C is incorrect and may result from dividing by the new price \((8 / 32 = 25\%)\). Choice D is incorrect and represents the new price as a percent of the original (\(32 / 40 = 80\%\)).

questions.questionHtml: If \(15\%\) of a number is 45, what is the number?
questions.explanationHtml:
Choice C is correct. Let the number be \(x\). Then \(0.15x = 45\). Solving, \(x = 45 \div 0.15 = 300\).

Choice A is incorrect and results from multiplying 45 by 0.15. Choice B is incorrect and may result from dividing 45 by 0.75. Choice D is incorrect and may result from multiplying 45 by 10.

questions.questionHtml: What number is \(25\%\) greater than 120?
questions.explanationHtml:
Choice C is correct. A number \(25\%\) greater than 120 is \(125\%\) of 120. As a decimal, \(125\% = 1.25\). Multiply: \(1.25 \times 120 = 150\). Alternate approach: \(25\%\) of 120 is 30, so \(120 + 30 = 150\).

Choice A is incorrect and results from subtracting \(25\%\) (\(120 - 30 = 90\)). Choice B is incorrect and may result from adding 25 to 120. Choice D is incorrect and may result from multiplying by 1.5.

questions.questionHtml: What number is \(30\%\) less than 200?
questions.explanationHtml:
Choice B is correct. A number \(30\%\) less than 200 is \(70\%\) of 200. \(70\% = 0.70\), so \(0.70 \times 200 = 140\). Alternate: \(30\%\) of 200 is 60, so \(200 - 60 = 140\).

Choice A is incorrect and is just \(30\%\) of 200. Choice C is incorrect and may result from subtracting 30 instead of \(30\%\). Choice D is incorrect and results from adding \(30\%\).

questions.questionHtml: A store increases the price of an item by \(10\%\), then decreases the new price by \(10\%\). What is the overall percent change from the original price?
questions.explanationHtml:
Choice B is correct. Let original price \(= 100\). After \(10\%\) increase: \(110\). After \(10\%\) decrease on \(110\): \(110 \times 0.10 = 11\), new price \(= 110 - 11 = 99\). Overall change \(= -1\), which is a \(1\%\) decrease.

Choice A is incorrect because successive percent changes do not cancel out unless applied to the same base. Choices C and D are incorrect as the net change is a \(1\%\) decrease.

questions.questionHtml: In a survey of 500 people, \(32\%\) said they prefer tea, \(28\%\) prefer coffee, and the rest prefer other drinks. How many people prefer other drinks?
questions.explanationHtml:
Choice C is correct. The percent who prefer other drinks \(= 100\% - (32\% + 28\%) = 40\%\). \(40\%\) of \(500 = 0.40 \times 500 = 200\).

Choice A is incorrect and may result from using \(28\%\) (\(0.28 \times 500 = 140\)). Choice B is incorrect and may result from using \(32\%\) (\(0.32 \times 500 = 160\)). Choice D is incorrect and may result from using \(60\%\) (300).

questions.questionHtml: The original price of a laptop is $800. It is discounted by \(15\%\) and then a \(7\%\) sales tax is added to the sale price. What is the final cost?
questions.explanationHtml:
Choice B is correct. First, discount: sale price \(= 85\%\) of $800 \(= 0.85 \times 800 = 680\). Then add 7% tax: tax \(= 0.07 \times 680 = 47.60\), so final cost \(= 680 + 47.60 = 727.60\).

Choice A is the sale price before tax. Choice C is incorrect and may result from applying tax to the original price (\(0.93 \times 800 = 744\)). Choice D is the original price.

questions.questionHtml: In 2019, a city had 240,000 residents. In 2020, the population increased by \(5\%\). In 2021, it decreased by \(5\%\) from the 2020 population. How many residents were there in 2021, and what is the percent change from 2019 to 2021?
questions.explanationHtml:
Choice B is correct. 2019: 240,000. 2020: increase \(5\% \rightarrow 240,000 \times 1.05 = 252,000\). 2021: decrease \(5\% \rightarrow 252,000 \times 0.95 = 239,400\). Overall change \(= 239,400 - 240,000 = -600\). Percent change \(= (-600 / 240,000) \times 100\% = -0.25\%\), a \(0.25\%\) decrease.

Choice A is incorrect because the two percent changes do not cancel. Choice C incorrectly shows increase. Choice D incorrectly increases both years.

questions.questionHtml: A survey found that \(45\%\) of the 620 residents in a town support a new park proposal. How many residents support the proposal?
questions.explanationHtml:
Choice A is correct. To find \(45\%\) of 620, convert \(45\%\) to decimal 0.45, then multiply: \(0.45 \times 620 = 279\).

Choice B is incorrect and may result from using \(50\%\) (310). Choice C is incorrect and may result from adding \(45 + 620\). Choice D is incorrect and may result from using \(65\%\) or miscalculation.

questions.questionHtml: The number of students at a school increased from 1,200 to 1,350 over one year. What was the percent increase?
questions.explanationHtml:
Choice B is correct. Percent increase \(= \frac{\text{new - original}}{\text{original}} \times 100\% = \frac{1350 - 1200}{1200} = \frac{150}{1200} = 0.125 = 12.5\%\).

Choice A is incorrect and may result from dividing by the new number (\(150 / 1350 \approx 11.1\%\)). Choice C is incorrect and may result from dividing by 1000. Choice D is incorrect and may result from dividing by 750.

questions.questionHtml: A laptop's price was reduced from $850 to $680 during a sale. What is the percent decrease?
questions.explanationHtml:
Choice B is correct. Percent decrease \(= \frac{\text{original - new}}{\text{original}} \times 100\% = \frac{850 - 680}{850} = \frac{170}{850} = 0.20 = 20\%\).

Choice A is incorrect (\(170/1133\)). Choice C is incorrect (\(170/680 = 25\%\) but that's dividing by the new price). Choice D is incorrect (\(170/567\)).

questions.questionHtml: After a \(15\%\) increase, a worker's salary is $4,600. What was the salary before the increase?
questions.explanationHtml:
Choice B is correct. Let original salary \(= x\). After \(15\%\) increase, salary \(= x \times 1.15 = 4600\). So \(x = 4600 \div 1.15 = 4000\).

Choice A is incorrect (subtracting \(15\%\) of 4600 incorrectly). Choice C is incorrect (\(4600/1.1\)). Choice D is incorrect (multiplying by 1.15).

questions.questionHtml: What number is \(18\%\) greater than 250?
questions.explanationHtml:
Choice C is correct. A number \(18\%\) greater than 250 is \(118\%\) of 250. \(118\% = 1.18\), so \(1.18 \times 250 = 295\). Alternate: \(18\%\) of \(250 = 45\), \(250 + 45 = 295\).

Choice A is incorrect \((250 + 18)\). Choice B is incorrect \((250 \times 1.08)\). Choice D is incorrect \((250 \times 1.2)\).

questions.questionHtml: In a school, \(60\%\) of the students are enrolled in a math club. Of those in the math club, \(25\%\) are also in the science club. What percentage of all students are in both clubs?
questions.explanationHtml:
Choice A is correct. Let total students \(= T\). Math club students \(= 0.60T\). Of these, \(25\%\) are in science club: \(0.25 \times (0.60T) = 0.15T\). That is \(15\%\) of all students.

Choice B is incorrect (maybe \(0.25 \times 0.8\)). Choice C is the percentage within math club. Choice D is sum \(60\% + 25\%\) incorrectly.

questions.questionHtml: A store raises the price of an item by \(20\%\), then later lowers the new price by \(20\%\). What is the net percent change from the original price?
questions.explanationHtml:
Choice B is correct. Assume original \(= 100\). After \(20\%\) increase: \(120\). After \(20\%\) decrease on \(120\): \(120 \times 0.20 = 24\), new price \(= 96\). Net change \(= -4\), which is a \(4\%\) decrease.

Choice A is incorrect because successive percent changes do not cancel. Choice C is incorrect (increase? no). Choice D is the single decrease percent.

questions.questionHtml: A car's value depreciates by \(15\%\) each year. If the car was purchased for $24,000, what is its estimated value after 3 years?
questions.explanationHtml:
Choice B is correct. Each year the car retains \(100\% - 15\% = 85\% = 0.85\) of its previous value. After 3 years: value \(= 24000 \times (0.85)^3 = 24000 \times 0.614125 = 14,739\) (rounded).

Choice A is too low (linear depreciation). Choice C is after 2 years (\(24000 \times 0.85^2 = 17,340\)). Choice D is after 1 year (\(24000 \times 0.85 = 20,400\)).

questions.questionHtml: 238 is \(85\%\) of what number?
questions.explanationHtml:
Choice B is correct. Let the number be \(x\). Then \(0.85x = 238\). So \(x = 238 \div 0.85 = 280\).

Choice A is \(85\%\) of 238. Choice C is \(238 \times 1.36\). Choice D is \(238 \div 0.68\).

questions.questionHtml: A jacket originally costs $120. It is first discounted by \(25\%\), then an additional \(10\%\) is taken off the discounted price. Finally, a \(6\%\) sales tax is added to the sale price. What is the final cost?
questions.explanationHtml:
Choice C is correct. First discount: \(25\%\) off \(\rightarrow\) pay \(75\%\) of $120 \(= 0.75 \times 120 = 90\). Second discount: \(10\%\) off 90 \(\rightarrow\) pay \(90\%\) of $90 \(= 0.90 \times 90 = 81\). Then add \(6\%\) tax: tax \(= 0.06 \times 81 = 4.86\), total \(= 81 + 4.86 = 85.86\).

Choice A is incorrect (perhaps applying discounts to original and tax on wrong base). Choice B is price after both discounts before tax. Choice D is incorrect (maybe \(25\%\) then \(10\%\) then tax added to original?).

questions.questionHtml: The number \(a\) is \(40\%\) less than the positive number \(b\). The number \(c\) is \(25\%\) greater than \(a\). What is the value of \(\frac{c}{b}\)?
questions.explanationHtml:
Choice B is correct. \(a\) is \(40\%\) less than \(b \rightarrow a = (1 - 0.40)b = 0.60b\). \(c\) is \(25\%\) greater than \(a \rightarrow c = (1 + 0.25)a = 1.25a\). Substitute: \(c = 1.25(0.60b) = 0.75b\). Thus \(\frac{c}{b} = 0.75\).

Choice A (0.65) might come from \(a = 0.6b\) and \(c = 1.25a\) incorrectly as \(1.25 \times 0.6 = 0.75\), so no; 0.65 is from \(0.6 + 0.05\). Choice C (0.85) from \(1.25 \times 0.68\). Choice D (1.05) from adding percents.

questions.questionHtml: The price of a stock increased from 2019 to 2020 by \(x\%\). From 2020 to 2021, the price increased by half that percent. If the overall percent increase from 2019 to 2021 was \(32\%\), what is the value of \(x\)?
questions.explanationHtml:
Choice C is correct. Let original price \(= P\). After first increase: \(P(1 + \frac{x}{100})\). After second increase of \(\frac{x}{2}\%\): \(P(1 + \frac{x}{100})(1 + \frac{x}{200}) = P(1 + \frac{32}{100}) = 1.32P\). Divide by \(P\): \((1 + \frac{x}{100})(1 + \frac{x}{200}) = 1.32\). Let \(t = \frac{x}{100}\). Then \((1 + t)(1 + \frac{t}{2}) = 1.32 \rightarrow 1 + 1.5t + 0.5t^2 = 1.32 \rightarrow 0.5t^2 +1.5t - 0.32 = 0 \rightarrow\) multiply by 2: \(t^2 + 3t - 0.64 = 0\). Solve: \(t = \frac{-3 \pm \sqrt{9 + 2.56}}{2} = \frac{-3 \pm \sqrt{11.56}}{2} = \frac{-3 \pm 3.4}{2}\). Positive: \(t = 0.4 / 2 = 0.2 \rightarrow x = 20\%\).

Choices A, B, D do not satisfy the equation.

questions.questionHtml: In a certain library, \(24\%\) of the books are fiction. Of the fiction books, \(75\%\) are hardcover. Of the hardcover fiction books, \(20\%\) are bestsellers. What percentage of all books in the library are hardcover fiction bestsellers?
questions.explanationHtml:
Choice B is correct. Let total books \(= T\). Fiction \(= 0.24T\). Hardcover fiction \(= 0.75 \times 0.24T = 0.18T\). Hardcover fiction bestsellers \(= 0.20 \times 0.18T = 0.036T = 3.6\%\) of \(T\).

Choice A \((1.2\%)\) is \(0.20 \times 0.24 \times 0.25\). Choice C \((15\%)\) is \(0.75 \times 0.20\). Choice D \((18\%)\) is just hardcover fiction without bestseller.

questions.questionHtml: A company surveyed employees about their preferred work mode. \(35\%\) preferred remote, \(40\%\) preferred hybrid, \(15\%\) preferred in-office, and the remaining 50 employees had no preference. How many more employees preferred hybrid than in-office?
questions.explanationHtml:
The correct answer is 125. The employees with no preference represent \(100\% - (35+40+15)\% = 10\%\) of total. So \(0.10 \times \text{Total} = 50 \rightarrow \text{Total} = 50 / 0.10 = 500\). Hybrid \(= 0.40 \times 500 = 200\). In-office \(= 0.15 \times 500 = 75\). Difference \(= 200 - 75 = 125\).

Choice B is the number of hybrid employees. Choice C is the number of in-office employees. Choice D is the number with no preference.

questions.questionHtml: The value of a painting increased by \(80\%\) from 2010 to 2015, then decreased by \(40\%\) from 2015 to 2020. What was the net percent change in the painting's value from 2010 to 2020?
questions.explanationHtml:
Choice A is correct. Let value in 2010 \(= V\). After \(80\%\) increase: \(V \times 1.80 = 1.8V\). After \(40\%\) decrease: multiply by \(1 - 0.40 = 0.60\), so value \(= 1.8V \times 0.60 = 1.08V\). That is an \(8\%\) increase from \(V\).

Choice B (8% decrease) would be 0.92V. Choice C (12% increase) would be 1.12V. Choice D (40% increase) is from adding \(80\% - 40\%\) incorrectly.

questions.questionHtml: The number \(p\) is \(30\%\) less than \(q\). The number \(r\) is \(50\%\) greater than \(p\). The number \(s\) is \(20\%\) less than \(r\). What is the value of \(\frac{s}{q}\)?
questions.explanationHtml:
The correct answer is 0.84. \(p = (1 - 0.30)q = 0.70q\). \(r = (1 + 0.50)p = 1.50 \times 0.70q = 1.05q\). \(s = (1 - 0.20)r = 0.80 \times 1.05q = 0.84q\). Thus \(s/q = 0.84\).

Choice B is \(p/q\). Choice C is \(r/q\). Choice D might come from multiplying 0.8 by 1.2 instead of 1.05.

questions.questionHtml:
The table below shows the results of a survey asking adults whether they exercise regularly.

Age groupExercise regularlyDo not exercise regularlyTotal
18-3412080200
35-54150100250
55+80120200

To the nearest whole percent, what is the difference between the percentage of adults aged 18-34 who exercise regularly and the percentage of adults aged 55+ who exercise regularly?
questions.explanationHtml:
Choice C is correct. For 18-34: exercise regularly \(= 120 / 200 = 0.60 = 60\%\). For 55+: \(80 / 200 = 0.40 = 40\%\). Difference \(= 20\) percentage points.

Choice A \((10\%)\) might be \(50\% - 40\%\). Choice B \((15\%)\) might be average. Choice D \((25\%)\) is \(60\% - 35\%\).

questions.questionHtml: A pharmaceutical company must ensure that a certain medication contains no more than \(0.0005\%\) of a particular impurity by mass. If a batch of the medication has a mass of 250 kilograms, what is the maximum mass, in grams, of the impurity allowed?
questions.explanationHtml:
The correct answer is 1.25 grams. \(0.0005\%\) means \(\frac{0.0005}{100} = 0.000005\) as a decimal. Maximum impurity mass = \(0.000005 \times 250\) kg = \(0.00125\) kg. Convert to grams: \(0.00125 \times 1000 = 1.25\) grams. (Note: common mistake is to forget to divide by 100 when converting percent to decimal.)

Choice B is the result without converting kg to grams. Choice C is multiplying by 1000 incorrectly. Choice D is a decimal misplacement.

questions.questionHtml: The number \(x\) is \(75\%\) greater than \(y\). The number \(y\) is \(60\%\) less than \(z\). The number \(z\) is \(20\%\) greater than 100. What is the value of \(x\)?
questions.explanationHtml:
Choice D is correct. Work backwards: \(z\) is \(20\%\) greater than \(100 \rightarrow z = 1.20 \times 100 = 120\). \(y\) is \(60\%\) less than \(z \rightarrow y = (1 - 0.60) \times 120 = 0.40 \times 120 = 48\). \(x\) is \(75\%\) greater than \(y \rightarrow x = 1.75 \times 48 = 84\).

Choice A (48) is just \(y\). Choice B (56) is \(1.75 \times 32\). Choice C (72) is \(1.5 \times 48\).

questions.questionHtml: The population of a town increased by \(25\%\) from 2015 to 2018, then decreased by \(10\%\) from 2018 to 2020, then increased by \(8\%\) from 2020 to 2023. What was the net percent change from 2015 to 2023?
questions.explanationHtml:
Choice B is correct. Let initial population \(= P\). After \(25\%\) increase: \(1.25P\). After \(10\%\) decrease: \(1.25P \times 0.90 = 1.125P\). After \(8\%\) increase: \(1.125P \times 1.08 = 1.215P\). Net multiplier \(= 1.215\) which is a \(21.5\%\) increase (since \(1.215 - 1 = 0.215\)).

Choice A \((20.15\%)\) would be from adding \(25 - 10 + 8 = 23\%\) then slight adjustment. Choice C \((23\%)\) is simple sum. Choice D \((24.3\%)\) is from multiplying incorrectly.
